plan.contextChunk: This figure shows cyclohexane in its chair form through three labeled panels, (a), (b), and (c). Panel (a) is a ball-and-stick model of the six-membered ring: six dark gray carbon spheres joined by pale rods trace a shape that rises at one end and dips at the other, each carbon carrying two off-white hydrogen spheres. Panel (b) redraws the same ring as a line structure with the near bonds bolded to signal depth, its carbons numbered 1 through 6 in magenta and its hydrogens lettered in magenta, green, blue, and black. Two drawn eyes at the right, marked "Observer", send magenta dashed sightlines to carbon 1 and to carbon 5. Panel (c) is the corresponding Newman projection: two circles, each with a front carbon dot and three bonds, are joined at the top and bottom by groups written "CH2", with the front atoms numbered 1 and 5 and the surrounding hydrogens numbered 2, 3, 4, and 6 in matching colors. Carrying the same numbering and hydrogen colors through all three panels lets the reader map any position on the model onto the corresponding position in the end-on view. Together the panels demonstrate that the chair shape holds its bond angles near the tetrahedral value while keeping every pair of neighboring C-H bonds staggered, leaving the ring free of strain.

right Newman projection circle representing the back carbon behind front carbon 5

front carbon dot at the center of the right Newman circle labeled 5 in magenta

interactions.label: Representation
interactions.teaches: The same cyclohexane chair can be read as a spatial model, as a chair line drawing, and as an end-on Newman projection without changing the underlying staggered bond relationships
Selecting carbon 1 or carbon 5 in the chair drawing reveals which front carbon, hydrogens, and CH2 connectors occupy the corresponding positions in the Newman projection

demo_steps.title: Start with the 3D chair
demo_steps.narration: The ball-and-stick model shows that cyclohexane is not flat: the six carbons form a chair, and each carbon carries one roughly axial and one roughly equatorial hydrogen.

demo_steps.title: Read the numbered chair drawing
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the line structure. The numbered carbons and colored hydrogens preserve the spatial relationships from the model while the bold bonds indicate the nearer edge being viewed.

demo_steps.title: Compare with the Newman projection
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the Newman projection to see the same C-H bonds end-on. The groups around each front carbon are staggered relative to the bonds on the carbon behind it.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use one visible panel at a time; do not show the three source panels simultaneously. Overall active figure should occupy about 7 world units wide by 4 world units tall. Ball-and-stick panel: carbon radius about 0.22, hydrogen radius about 0.14, bond cylinder radius about 0.045. C-C bond length about 1.0; C-H bond length about 0.72. Approximate carbon coordinates for the chair model, before camera rotation: C1=(1.35,-0.45,0.55), C2=(0.35,-0.85,-0.45), C3=(-0.85,-0.45,0.55), C4=(-1.35,0.45,-0.45), C5=(-0.35,0.85,0.55), C6=(0.85,0.45,-0.45). Draw C-C bonds C1-C2-C3-C4-C5-C6-C1. Add one axial hydrogen per carbon alternating up/down relative to the chair and one equatorial hydrogen projecting outward; the source view has several axial hydrogens nearly vertical on screen and equatorial hydrogens angled outward. Ball-and-stick colors: carbons dark gray #566466, hydrogens off-white #dce1d1, bonds pale blue-gray #9fb3bf, with soft highlights. Line-structure panel is mostly a flat XY drawing on z=0: set C3=(-2.2,-0.55), C4=(-1.75,0.65), C5=(-0.45,0.42), C6=(0.8,0.85), C1=(0.45,-0.55), C2=(-0.85,-0.42). Draw the ring in order 1-2-3-4-5-6-1. The source has C1 at the lower right of the chair drawing, C5 near the upper center, C6 at upper right, C4 at upper left, C3 lower left, and C2 lower middle. Make bonds C1-C2 and C1-C6 thick black to read as the nearer edge; keep the left and upper-left bonds thinner. Place the observer eyes to the right of the line structure at about x=3.0, y=0.1, with the word Observer centered below at y=-1.45. Magenta dashed sightlines #ff1493 run diagonally from the eyes leftward to C1 and C5. Number labels are magenta #ff1493. Hydrogen text colors: magenta #ff1493 for the highlighted top hydrogens, green #009966 for side hydrogens, blue #008fd3 for lower hydrogens, black #111111 for black hydrogens. Newman panel: flat XY drawing on z=0. Left Newman circle center=(-1.15,0.15), radius=0.55; right circle center=(1.15,0.15), radius=0.55. Each front carbon is a small black dot at circle center with magenta labels 1 and 5 placed just above or beside the dot. Left front carbon 1 bonds: vertical up to magenta H, vertical down to blue H, upper-right toward the upper CH2 bridge. Left rear bonds emerge from the circle edge in staggered positions, including green H at upper-left and green H at lower-left, plus a lower-right connection toward the lower CH2 group. Right front carbon 5 mirrors this: vertical up to magenta H, vertical down to blue H, upper-left toward the upper CH2 bridge; rear bonds include green H at upper-right and black/green side hydrogens, plus lower-left connection to lower CH2. Upper CH2 connector spans between the two circles above them, labeled CH2 in black with magenta number 6 nearby. Lower CH2 connector spans between the circles below or slightly between them, labeled CH2 with magenta number 3 nearby. Keep all Newman C-H bonds staggered by about 60 degrees around each circle.
interactionPlan.notes: Implement the three representations as separate scene groups and switch visibility with representationView. The line structure and Newman projection should be rendered with orthographic-looking text and line overlays inside the perspective scene so labels remain legible. Use CSS2D or signed-distance-field text for H, CH2, numbers, panel labels, and Observer. The click interaction should create persistent selection state for carbon 1 or carbon 5: in the line view, highlight the chosen numbered carbon and its attached bonds; in the Newman view, highlight the corresponding left or right front carbon dot, the front C-H bonds, adjacent hydrogens, and the CH2 connector bonds. If the learner clicks carbon 1 in the line drawing and then toggles to Newman projection, keep the carbon 1 highlight active.

authoredContext:
Cyclohexane adopts a strain-free, three-dimensional shape that is called a chair conformation because of its similarity to a lounge chair, with a back, seat, and footrest (the figure). Chair cyclohexane has neither angle strain nor torsional strain—all C−C−C bond angles are near the 109° tetrahedral value, and all neighboring C−H bonds are staggered.

The strain-free chair conformation of cyclohexane. All C−C−C bond angles are 111.5°, close to the ideal 109° tetrahedral angle, and all neighboring C−H bonds are staggered.

The ball and stick model, chair conformation, and Newman projection of cyclohexane. The carbon atoms are numbered in chair conformation and Newman projection.

The easiest way to visualize chair cyclohexane is to build a molecular model if you have access to a model kit, or alternatively to explore with one of the many computer-based modeling programs you may have access to.
